title: Classify radical pencil reachability by characteristic-polynomial splitting (no new κ)
body:
## Summary

Scoped algebraic proof with finite corroboration. For every field K, every n>=1 and A in M_n(K), over R=K[x,y]/(x,y)^2 in the paid alphabet I+u v^T with v over K and arbitrary free GL_n(K) maps:

```text
xI+yA is reachable  <=>  char_A splits over K.
If reachable, exact paid cost = n.
```

This answers Open next question 1 of #4773. A scalar eigenvalue is insufficient: the binary matrix diag(0, companion(t^2+t+1)) has an unreachable pencil. Among all 512 binary three-role pencils, exactly 352 are reachable and 160 are excluded, including 112 with a scalar eigenvalue that the predecessor obstruction did not exclude. No new kappa, supplier admission, selected-frontier change or complete multiplication theorem is claimed.

The necessity proof lifts the literal finite word to K[X,Y]. Each paid determinant is affine linear, while the endpoint forces its first nonzero homogeneous determinant to be det(XI+YA). Thus this homogeneous determinant splits, regardless of word length. A full invariant flag supplies an attaining n-factor column-replacement word.

Only `research/split-radical-pencil/` is added. Produced by Nick Petalas. Credit Nick Petalas #4773/#4745/#4243, Wentao Li #4099 following #2513, and ToikY #4334 for the predecessor question, alphabet and radical results. Determinant multiplicativity, the rank-one determinant identity and triangularization are classical. No predecessor executable is imported or audited.

## Evidence

- Before: #4773 proves an eigenvalue necessary condition and explicitly leaves its sufficiency open.
- After: the written all-field, all-role classification distinguishes complete splitting from existence of one eigenvalue and proves exact cost n.
- Every matrix in seven finite domains passes independent characteristic-polynomial/root-division and constructive invariant-flag criteria: 23,574 targets over F2,F3,F4,F5,F7. Every split case passes a literal paid-word matrix identity with free conjugation. Three-role binary counts are 352 split, 112 rootful nonsplit, 48 rootless; three-role ternary counts are 9,909 split, 6,318 rootful nonsplit, 3,456 rootless.
- All 512 dirty binary inputs pass a nontrivial three-role word. Nine odd-field polynomial-lift evaluations and nine control cases pass. The controls include the rootful nonsplit witness, singular A, chronology reversal, each omitted factor, an odd-field sign, the nonprime field law and an irreducible polynomial.
- Both registered commands passed locally with warnings treated as errors, timed separately at 2.20 s and 2.19 s. The package runner passed. Five-file committed-byte/source-history preflight, committed export integrity and optimized replay from a read-only Git-free export with PATH=/nonexistent passed at `0764ab259a8ce496a4c5d4debeed4c4e4d9f7ca4`. Export replay took 2.22 s. Normal, optimized and exported generated receipts agree completely and bind all five package files. No receipt is hand-written.


Any CPython 3.12 installation can replace the displayed interpreter path. Expected marker: `PASS_SPLIT_RADICAL_PENCIL binary_three_role=352/512 rootful_excluded=112 no_new_kappa`.

Canonical main is pinned at `624de9dc66858af0945e5f8a0942488d62280d43`, priority revision 7, and was fetched again before committing. Current selected source-binding orientation passed after materializing omitted sparse sources; this is metadata orientation only. TASK.json explicitly changes the historical formal-interface card to this algebraic side question. Live claims, open PR bodies, distinctive merged searches and main README terms were rechecked before the commit. The overlap helper reported complete remote pagination and incomplete sparse local-note coverage, which does not certify novelty.

[Advance claim](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-19131512).

## Limitations and unrun obligations

The universal result is the written scoped proof, corroborated by bounded finite checks. The algebra has exactly two independent square-zero radical generators, the first pencil coefficient is I, and right vectors/free maps are over the central field. Arbitrary radical matrices, higher nilpotency, restored auxiliary roles and ring-valued free maps are not classified. Independent human and formal proof-kernel review are unclaimed.

Native coefficient preparation, routing, restoration, precision, stock and complete supplier costs remain unknown. Lean, Docker and the selected operator replay were outside scope and were not run. Every registered local command ran successfully.

## Open next questions

- Classify xB+yC when B is singular, beginning with a fixed Kronecker singular block. An identically zero homogeneous determinant leaves the present criterion incomplete.
- For three or more independent square-zero generators, determine whether a split homogeneous determinant is sufficient. Start with an invertible first coefficient and two other coefficient matrices; simultaneous flags may carry additional information.

## Related open work

No open PR studying this radical-pencil family or its reachability count was found in the pre-commit full overlap snapshot or targeted live right-vector/radical PR searches. Other active claims concern invertible local targets, matrix-algebra rank-two targets, nonzero rank-one residue lifts, product algebras and polynomial coefficient algebras. Their endpoint domains differ from this zero-residue two-generator pencil family; no overlapping numerical total is asserted.

Merged #4773 is the direct predecessor. Its 48 binary three-role eigenvalue-free pencils agree numerically with the 48 rootless cases here, while the 112 rootful nonsplit exclusions and 352/512 complete classification are new. Merged #4745/#4766 classify/count all two-role square-zero radical matrices; this result answers a larger-role pencil question rather than rerunning their census.

### Related open work refresh before DONE

This account's open PRs created since the CLAIM at 2026-10-22T19:44:31Z were listed before DONE. The newer same-alphabet work is:

- #4780, head `a4436fab4164eccc498d4d9885eec68211c869de`, proves a singular rank-one threshold over pure field products K^k. Its coefficient algebra differs from this local square-zero algebra, so no endpoint count or threshold overlaps.
- #4781, head `b838121c65e1bfd17a65466c95940eb00f12a225`, counts lifts of nonzero rank-one residues over proper residue-field extensions. Our pencils have zero residue. Its 567 one-factor lifts and our 352 reachable binary pencils count disjoint sets; no overlapping number is asserted.
- #4784, head `4d0a6363fe4f45dd9a769f5b74d02fc5d9061ae3`, gives invertible polynomial-target cost distributions over F_q[t]. Both the coefficient algebra and invertible endpoint differ, so no target or count overlaps.
- #4787, head `4b58e8cd5690bd35cf01b0018eefa2c39a298920`, proves exact costs for invertible local-algebra targets at arbitrary role counts. Its samples include the same binary square-zero coefficient algebra, but its invertible endpoints and our zero-residue endpoints are disjoint. No cost or census is asserted on a shared target.

- #4789, head `7fdbf8040ea9a957af0576067df2d9cb6fcf0e51`, classifies ordinary rank-two targets over matrix algebras M_m(K), m>=3. Those noncommutative matrix coefficients differ from this scalar-residue local square-zero algebra, so no target or census count overlaps.

The titles and full bodies of these five PRs were read. Other newly open account PRs concern Schur dimensions and full-guard probabilities. No conflicting overlapping number was found within this coverage.
